topics.title: Chapter 1 — Linux and the System Administrator
topics.summary: HarborWorks has received a virtual server for a new internal website. Someone can log in, and a web page appears. The team calls the server finished. Then the machine restarts, the website disappears, and nobody knows who owns the account that originally launched it. The missing piece was not another command. It was a model of what the operating system does and what an administrator is responsible for preserving.

topics.title: 1.1 What Is Linux?
topics.summary: Linux is the kernel at the center of many operating systems. In everyday speech, people also use “Linux” to mean a complete system containing that kernel, libraries, commands, services, and an installer. Keep both meanings in mind. A statement about the Linux scheduler concerns the kernel; a statement about the default package manager usually concerns a distribution.

blocks.text: Linux is the kernel at the center of many operating systems. In everyday speech, people also use “Linux” to mean a complete system containing that kernel, libraries, commands, services, and an installer. Keep both meanings in mind. A statement about the Linux scheduler concerns the kernel; a statement about the default package manager usually concerns a distribution.

An operating system shares hardware among programs and provides common services. A program asks to open a file rather than directly driving a storage controller. It asks for memory rather than choosing physical memory chips. These services make programs practical to write, while permissions and isolation limit how much one program can affect another.

For administration, the useful question is not simply “Does it run Linux?” Ask which distribution, release, kernel, architecture, service manager, and package sources are present. That information changes which repair procedure is appropriate. Read /etc/os-release for distribution identity and uname -r for the running kernel. Neither output replaces the other. (R01, R03)
Linux example — 1.1
Identify the distribution and running kernel separately.

cat /etc/os-release
uname -r

topics.title: 1.2 The Linux Kernel
topics.summary: The kernel manages processes, memory, devices, filesystems, and networking. It runs with privileges unavailable to ordinary applications. A system call is a controlled entry point through which a program requests a kernel operation. Reading a file, creating a process, and opening a network socket all eventually depend on kernel services.

blocks.text: The kernel manages processes, memory, devices, filesystems, and networking. It runs with privileges unavailable to ordinary applications. A system call is a controlled entry point through which a program requests a kernel operation. Reading a file, creating a process, and opening a network socket all eventually depend on kernel services.

This division explains why a failed application does not always indicate a failed kernel. A website might return an error because its configuration names the wrong directory. The kernel may be correctly refusing access. Replacing the kernel would not address the cause.

Kernel behavior is influenced by compiled features, loaded modules, boot parameters, and runtime settings. You will inspect these in Chapter 24. For now, record the running version and avoid assuming that an installed kernel package is already active. A package update can place new kernel files on disk while the old kernel continues to run until reboot.
Linux example — 1.2
Inspect kernel identity and its boot arguments.

uname -a
cat /proc/cmdline
blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: What to check: The arguments describe this boot, not every installed kernel.

blocks.text: User space is where ordinary applications and most administration tools run. Bash interprets commands; utilities such as cp, sort, and chmod perform focused operations; libraries provide shared code. Many familiar tools come from the GNU project, although a Linux system may use other implementations.

The practical consequence is that “the same command” can differ across environments. A minimal container may provide BusyBox utilities instead of GNU utilities. An option copied from a workstation might therefore be unavailable. Use command -v tool, tool --help, and the installed manual rather than guessing which implementation is present.

A shell pipeline works because these tools exchange byte streams through standard input and output. The kernel supplies processes and pipes; user-space programs supply the text transformations. Learning this separation makes the command line less mysterious and helps you locate failures precisely.
Linux example — 1.3
Find the programs Bash will execute.

command -v bash cp sort chmod
cp --version

Two distributions can share major components yet differ in package names, service units, security policy, and release timing.

blocks.text: A distribution assembles the kernel, user-space software, repositories, update policy, configuration defaults, and support documentation into a usable operating system. Two distributions can share major components yet differ in package names, service units, security policy, and release timing.

Choose a distribution by workload needs, support expectations, staff familiarity, hardware compatibility, and lifecycle requirements. A familiar administration interface is valuable, but so is having a supported path for security updates. “Newest” is not a complete operating requirement.

Do not mix repositories from unrelated releases to obtain one desired package. The package manager reasons about a compatible set of dependencies. Replacing part of that set with incompatible libraries can break applications that were not part of your original change. Prefer a supported package, a separately isolated application environment, or a planned operating-system upgrade.
Linux example — 1.4
Read the distribution's identity fields.
cat /etc/os-release

blocks.text: Debian and Ubuntu use the DEB package format and APT tools for repository-based installation. They share many conventions, but they are not interchangeable releases of one product. Ubuntu builds on Debian work while making its own packaging, release, and support choices.

A common administrative split is apt for interactive work and apt-get for scripts that need a more stable command interface. Configuration generally lives under /etc, while package metadata records which files belong to installed software. Ubuntu commonly uses AppArmor for mandatory access controls, a topic introduced in Chapter 17.
On a new host, inspect rather than assume:

cat /etc/os-release
command -v apt apt-get dpkg
systemctl --version
blocks.code:
cat /etc/os-release
command -v apt apt-get dpkg
systemctl --version
blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: Record both the release identity and the installed tools. A container image based on Ubuntu may not run systemd as PID 1, even though a full Ubuntu server normally does. Distribution identity alone does not describe the execution environment.
Linux example — 1.5
On Debian or Ubuntu, inspect the package tools.

command -v apt apt-get dpkg
dpkg-query -W bash

The transferable skill is recognizing responsibilities. Every system needs package trust, network configuration, service supervision, identity, storage, and recovery. The specific tool names are an implementation detail that must still be checked carefully.

When moving a procedure between distributions, make a translation sheet: package name, configuration path, service name, firewall manager, mandatory-access-control system, and validation command. Translating only the installation command leaves the dangerous differences hidden. (R04)

topics.title: 1.8 Desktop Linux vs. Server Linux
topics.summary: Desktop and server installations can use the same kernel while selecting different packages and defaults. A desktop emphasizes interactive sessions, displays, audio, removable devices, and user convenience. A server emphasizes unattended operation, controlled remote access, predictable startup, and maintained services.

blocks.text: Desktop and server installations can use the same kernel while selecting different packages and defaults. A desktop emphasizes interactive sessions, displays, audio, removable devices, and user convenience. A server emphasizes unattended operation, controlled remote access, predictable startup, and maintained services.

A graphical interface is not inherently incompatible with a server, but unnecessary software increases update work and the number of components that can fail. Install what the service and its operators need, not every package that might be convenient someday.

The reverse mistake is stripping a server so aggressively that recovery tools are unavailable. A minimal image should still have a documented method for inspecting networking, storage, logs, and package state. “Minimal” should mean intentional, not unmaintainable.
Linux example — 1.8
On a systemd host, compare the boot target with running services.

systemctl get-default
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager

topics.summary: An administrator maintains the conditions under which services work safely and predictably. That includes installation, access control, updates, monitoring, backup recovery, capacity, documentation, and incident response. It also includes deciding when not to make a change.

blocks.text: An administrator maintains the conditions under which services work safely and predictably. That includes installation, access control, updates, monitoring, backup recovery, capacity, documentation, and incident response. It also includes deciding when not to make a change.

Consider a request to “fix permissions” by making an application directory writable by everyone. The administrator must identify the actual service identity, determine which files need writes, and preserve restrictions on executable code. Following the requested command literally can violate the real requirement.

Good administration produces evidence. A restore test demonstrates recoverability; a second SSH session demonstrates continued access; an application request demonstrates useful service. A command returning zero is evidence about that command, not automatically about the whole system. The professional habit is connecting the narrow observation to the broader outcome.
Linux example — 1.9
Collect a small operational snapshot.

date -Is
uptime
df -h /

blocks.text: A physical server runs on dedicated hardware. A virtual machine sees virtual hardware supplied by a hypervisor. A cloud instance is typically a VM or another compute abstraction provisioned through a provider’s control plane. All can run similar Linux user-space software while exposing different failure boundaries.

On physical hardware, you may manage firmware, disks, power, and remote management controllers. With VMs, you also depend on the host’s storage and resource scheduling. In the cloud, identity permissions, virtual networking, metadata, quotas, and provider lifecycle events become part of the operating environment.

An in-guest tool cannot reveal every underlying cause. High latency might originate in the guest, the hypervisor, shared storage, or a provider limit. Record which layers your team owns and which require another team or provider. Ownership boundaries belong in the runbook before an incident.

topics.summary: Production is an environment on which real users or business processes depend. It is defined by consequences, not by the hostname containing prod. A small payroll script can be production even when it runs on an old workstation.

blocks.text: Production is an environment on which real users or business processes depend. It is defined by consequences, not by the hostname containing prod. A small payroll script can be production even when it runs on an old workstation.

Production work needs explicit requirements for availability, data loss, recovery time, access, change approval, and support ownership. A development shortcut becomes dangerous when nobody notices that its assumptions no longer hold. A local snapshot, for example, may help development resets but cannot protect against loss of the host that stores it.

Before changing a production machine, determine the affected service, expected impact, evidence of a current backup, validation steps, and rollback conditions. The goal is not paperwork for its own sake. It is ensuring that a second administrator can understand the change and recover the service when the original operator is unavailable.
Linux example — 1.11
Observe production health without changing state.

systemctl --failed --no-pager
findmnt /
uptime

Use official installation media, verify its published checksum or signature through a trusted channel, and keep the hypervisor’s console available. Use an ordinary named account with controlled sudo access rather than working permanently as root.

Create a clean snapshot only after installing updates and confirming login. Then record the VM name, operating-system release, virtual network, disk identities, and credentials-storage location. Do not place passwords in the notebook itself.

Start with isolated networking. Package downloads may use NAT, but inbound services should remain on the lab network. Add a disposable disk later for Chapters 9 and 10. Confirm the ability to power off, revert a snapshot, and boot recovery media before intentionally breaking anything. A lab is complete when its recovery path works, not merely when its installation finishes.

blocks.text: date -Is produces a timestamp including an offset. hostname identifies the current name, not necessarily the authoritative inventory record. uname -m identifies the machine architecture. id shows the credentials of this session. The PID 1 query reveals whether systemd, a container entrypoint, or another process occupies that role.

lsblk displays block-device relationships; it does not approve any device for erasure. ip -br address summarizes interfaces and assigned addresses; it does not prove end-to-end connectivity. These limits are part of the result.

It is not to force APT onto the machine because a spreadsheet expected Ubuntu.

topics.title: Practice and implementation lab
topics.summary: Create a host identity sheet for each lab VM. Include the distribution, release, running kernel, architecture, PID 1, primary IP address, and recovery-console method. Then compare the two sheets and identify three commands that work on both systems and two management choices that differ.

blocks.text: Create a host identity sheet for each lab VM. Include the distribution, release, running kernel, architecture, PID 1, primary IP address, and recovery-console method. Then compare the two sheets and identify three commands that work on both systems and two management choices that differ.

Reboot one VM from its normal operating-system interface. Reconnect and repeat the identity checks. Explain which values should remain stable and which may change. A DHCP address can change; a distribution should not change merely because the machine rebooted.

Check your understanding. Why is uname -r insufficient to select a package command? Because it reports the running kernel, not the complete distribution’s package-management policy. Why is a VM snapshot not automatically a backup? Because it can share storage and failure modes with the original VM. What makes a server production? Real dependence and consequences, not its size or name.
Chapter takeaway. Identify the environment, establish ownership, and prove a recovery path before making changes. Every later procedure assumes these foundations.
